title: Vault ↔ Purview Coexistence — eDiscovery, Legal Hold & Retention
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: Keep eDiscovery and retention defensible across both ecosystems
problem: During coexistence, legal and compliance must be able to hold, retain, and discover data across both Microsoft Purview and Google Vault — a gap here is a legal risk. This solution designs the Vault ↔ Purview coexistence for eDiscovery, legal hold, and retention: what's governed where, how holds/retention map across ecosystems, and how to run defensible discovery during the transition, deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the dual-ecosystem governance model: what data lives in Purview vs Vault during coexistence, and how holds/retention/discovery are coordinated.
Requirements Guide — prerequisites (Vault-capable Workspace edition, Purview access, legal/eDiscovery stakeholders, retention policy, a pilot) with how to verify/implement each.
Implementation Guide — exact steps to configure Google Vault retention/holds, map to Purview during coexistence, define the discovery workflow across both, validate on a pilot, then expand.
5 supporting scripts — retention/hold discovery across the estate, per-scope retention/hold validation, a coverage/gap report, safe remediation, and a scope helper.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (holds effective, retention applied, discovery returns) plus Best Practices for defensible eDiscovery.
short: Design Vault ↔ Purview coexistence for eDiscovery, legal hold, and retention — what's governed where and how holds/retention map across ecosystems — so discovery stays defensible during the transition, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
